description: One long quill that shifts through every colour as it turns. No bird anyone has flushed grows these.
lore: Sixty gold buys a great many fakes. The usual method is a common quill, four dyes and a patient afternoon, and it is good enough at a lamplit stall to have taken most people at least once. The test costs nothing: turn it slowly. A dyed feather goes through its colours one at a time. A true one holds two at once, and the seam between them slides. The woman who taught [[lore/the_hard_pieces|the trade]] that test made the fakes for eleven years, says so freely, and is paid now to stand at the far end of the table looking bored.
gm_notes: The counterfeiter turned inspector: a face for the junk market whenever a scene needs one. The turning test is real and usable at the table.
